headline: Apple has launched HomeView, a $299 smart display with a 7-inch screen, to push its AI-upgraded Siri assistant into the home.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a launch by one of the world's biggest consumer technology makers, confirmed and covered with analyst doubts, but a product launch rather than a breakthrough.
importance_line: Apple's $299 home screen goes on sale next month, but not in the EU, it needs a recently unlocked iPhone to reach private data, and analysts doubt that Siri, upgraded this summer with Google's help, is strong enough to win a crowded market.
summary: Reuters reports that Apple on 13 Oct 2026 launched HomeView, a $299 smart display with a 7-inch screen and face recognition that can control doorbells, thermostats and smart locks and starts shipping next month, alongside updated HomePod and Apple TV devices and accessories from LG and Schneider Electric. This follows CNET's 11 Oct 2026 report that Apple's smart home hub was reportedly called HomeView and would ship in November; new today are Apple's confirmation, the price and its statement that the device will not be sold in the European Union because Siri AI remains unavailable there under EU regulations.
notes: Reuters page itself returned HTTP 401; the Reuters wire text was read on its copy at Euronext (https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/apple-bets-new-screen-gadget-siri-ai-home-device-push) and checked against the same text on BNN Bloomberg.
